# K06. X9 (x9step3): fused AdamW master-weight step, gradient-norm pass and weight-amax epilogue (Triton)

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switches: `AK_X9_E0=1` (config L20), `AK_X9_FOLD=1` (config L20), `AK_X9_WAMAX=1` (config L20) · In the submitted runs: **on** · Class: **E0-restricted** (norm pass; the step E0) · Rule basis: Hyperparameters, optimizer paragraph (TR-9.1c); Numerical formats (TR-5.2b) for gradient clipping; Graph Execution (TR-8.3)

**L4 v3.** This item is L4 v2's, byte for byte, in L4 v3's image. Where this write-up names L4 v2's results, image or test runs, that evidence was collected on L4 v2's package (`firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v2`, withdrawn from this submission; see [Index](../KERNELS.md)). This package's own ten runs print the same K6 ARMED lines and the same epilogue check, `True` (Evidence).

## In brief

NVIDIA's recipe runs the optimizer step as Megatron-Core's distributed optimizer with Transformer Engine's (TE's)
`FusedAdam` in AdamW mode: fp32 gradient copies, norm, clip scaling, AdamW update of fp32 masters and moments, bf16
copy. K6 (X9) does the same work in two Triton passes that read the bf16 gradients directly: a norm pass in TE's exact
reduction order, and a fused step that applies the clip coefficient and TE's AdamW arithmetic operation for operation,
writes the bf16 parameters and each weight's maximum |value| for the next NVFP4 weight quantize (the "epilogue"). Every
operation, rounding and order is TE's, except that the norm pass keeps fp32 subnormal partial sums that TE flushes to 0:
**E0-restricted** for the norm, E0 for the AdamW step. The step has no run-time first-call check; its equality rests on
192 comparisons with TE's and apex's `FusedAdam` (0 differing bytes), six closed loops of 2,002 optimizer steps (E0)
and in-training shadows (0 mismatches).

## What it replaces (Replaces)

Megatron-Core's `DistributedOptimizer` keeps an fp32 "master" copy of every bf16 weight, sharded across the
data-parallel ranks: each rank owns one contiguous range (a "shard") of each parameter's elements and updates only that.
With TE's `FusedAdam` (AdamW mode), each optimizer step runs, per rank: (1) fp32 copies of the bf16 gradient shards
(Megatron's `copy_group_grads`, from `main_grad`, bf16 here); (2) the local L2 norm, TE's `multi_tensor_l2norm` over
the copies, through `multi_tensor_applier`; (3) the clip scaling, TE's `multi_tensor_scale_tensor` (every fp32 gradient
times the clip coefficient, a device tensor); (4) the update, TE's `multi_tensor_adam` on the fp32 master weights and
the moments m and v; (5) the bf16 parameter copy (each master shard rounded into the bf16 parameter buffer). K6
replaces all five, and folds into its epilogue the separate weight-amax pass of the next NVFP4 weight quantize (K9's
shard pass, `multi_amax_bf16`).

## Why the result is the same (Equivalence)

The chain K6 replaces, per rank and per parameter group (NVIDIA's, plus K9's shard pass for the weight amaxes), then K6
with N5's wiring:

```
g32    = fp32(g_bf16)                          Megatron copy_group_grads (exact)
n_loc  = multi_tensor_l2norm(g32)              TE (fast-math build)
total  = sqrt(all_reduce_sum(n_loc²))          Megatron get_grad_norm_fp32
c      = min(1, max_norm / (total + 1e-6))     Megatron clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32
g32    = g32 · c                               TE multi_tensor_scale_tensor
p,m,v  = multi_tensor_adam(g32, p, m, v)       TE FusedAdam, AdamW mode
p_bf16 = bf16(p)                               Megatron's copy of the masters into the bf16 parameter buffer
amax[slot] = max over the shard of |p_bf16|    K9's shard pass (multi_amax_bf16), not NVIDIA's

n_loc  = norm(g_bf16)                          K6 norm pass: TE's reduction order, reading the bf16 bits
total, c                                       unchanged; c is stashed for the step, not applied by a scale pass
per element:  ĝ = c · fp32(g);  m, v, p as TE;  p_bf16 = bf16(p);
              amax[slot] = max(amax[slot], |p_bf16|)          K6 fused step with its epilogue
```

- **Reading bf16 directly.** `fp32(g_bf16)` is exact (the 16 bits shifted into the top of an fp32 word; module
  L186-189), so both passes see the values TE sees in the fp32 copies.
- **Norm.** TE's reduction order, step for step (module L11-26, L127-338): 65,536-element chunks; 512 lanes with 4
  accumulators each, combined as `((a0+a1)+a2)+a3`; the block tree over the 512 lanes, pairs (t, t+256), (t, t+128), …,
  (0, 1), each a sum of exactly two numbers; at most 320 blocks and 110 tensors per launch, each block's result in one
  of 320 slots; the cleanup that adds the slots launch by launch and runs the same tree; `sqrt.approx`. A lane takes
  TE's aligned-path elements when the shard's length is a multiple of 4 and the strided-path elements otherwise, as TE
  does on the fresh fp32 copies (module L579-584). So the local norm has TE's bytes outside the domain below.
- **Clip.** `ĝ = c · fp32(g)` is the same single fp32 multiply (`mul.rn.ftz`) that TE's scale kernel applies to the
  fp32 copies the stock step then reads.
- **Step.** TE's per-element fp32 chain, operation for operation, with TE's host scalars (module L106-123, L368-379
  and L413-424; equations under Optimizer). **bf16 parameters:** round to nearest even, as Megatron's copy.
- **Epilogue.** The maximum of |bf16(p)| over each shard, from the bit pattern: `bits & 0x7FFF`, a NaN (> `0x7F80`)
  counted as 0, subnormals and infinities kept (`multi_amax_bf16`'s arithmetic; module L345-348, L385-392, L430-435).
  Each program folds its maximum into the weight's slot with an integer atomic max of `value << 16` on an int32 view of
  the fp32 amax buffer, which the caller zeroes first. For non-negative floats the integer order of the bit patterns is
  the numeric order, and a maximum does not depend on operand order, so the result equals the separate shard pass
  whatever order the atomics land in.

### Class: E0-restricted

E0-restricted means byte-identical except on a stated input domain. Here the domain concerns the norm pass only.

- **The AdamW step** (master, m, v, bf16 parameter) and the epilogue's amaxes: E0, byte-identical on every graded case,
  including fp32 subnormals and `−0.0` masters at learning rate 0.
- **The norm pass and the clip coefficient:** byte-identical on every graded case. The norm can differ from TE's only on
  this domain: some partial sum in the norm pass's evaluation (a lane's accumulator, a node of a block tree, or a slot's
  running sum) is a non-zero subnormal that TE's fast-math kernel flushes to 0. That needs every non-zero gradient
  element feeding that partial sum to satisfy |g| < 2^-63, because the square of any larger value is at least 2^-126,
  the smallest normal fp32 (record R15).
- **Why training stays outside it.** An exactly zero gradient (for example an embedding row of a token absent from the
  step, of either sign) adds +0 and leaves a partial sum at +0, outside the domain. Once one element with |g| ≥ 2^-63
  feeds a partial sum, that sum and every sum built on it are normal for the rest of the evaluation, since the pass adds
  only non-negative squares. Entering the domain therefore needs every non-zero element accumulated so far into a
  partial sum (at most 32 elements per lane accumulator in a full 65,536-element chunk, fewer in a ragged tail) to lie
  below 2^-63, about 1.1 × 10^-19.
- **No compared case or step showed a difference in the norm:** the in-training shadows (16 of 16 steps of the 2 × 4
  run, 36 steps per rank at DP 8), the closed loops (every one of 2,002 steps, six loops) and the call-site verifier's 17
  cases, including subnormal-gradient cases (Evidence).

**State kept between calls:** the kernels keep no data between calls. The `FusedAdamWMaster` object caches its launch
and address tables (module L500-547, L549-637), the norm's partial-sum buffer of 320 slots per launch (L634; the finish
kernel reads only slots the chunk kernel wrote in the same call), the 1-element norm output, overwritten every call
(L495, L649-651), and the slot tensor (L662-665). The hook caches the gradient views and one fused instance per
parameter group and phase, with its lists (patch `mcore/0001` L127-136, L191-250), the weight-amax slot lists
(L283-301), and the clip coefficient, stashed every step (L184-187; patch `mcore/0002` L75-76), asserted present (patch
`mcore/0001` L262) and cleared after every fused step (L106-108). The master weights, m and v are the optimizer's own
state, updated in place (read from `fused_adamw_master.py` L464-685 and patch `mcore/0001` L97-301).

## Numerics (Numerics)

- fp32 master weights, m and v; bf16 parameters (round to nearest even).
- The step's per-element chain is inline PTX (module L64-93): `mul.rn.ftz`, `fma.rn.ftz`, `add.rn.ftz`,
  `div.full.ftz`, `sqrt.approx.ftz`. TE compiles its multi-tensor kernels with `--use_fast_math`, so its operations are
  these. FTZ (flush subnormal inputs and results to zero) is required for byte equality with stock, not a deviation.
- `−lr` is a true negation (`lr · −1.0`; Triton's `-lr` is `0 − lr`, which is +0 for lr = 0, module L379, L424), so
  lr = 0 in the warm-up does not flip `−0.0` master weights.
- **The norm kernels are not FTZ.** They use plain Triton `fma`, `+` and two-element sums (module L190-193, L207-208,
  L130-138, L335); only the step kernels received the FTZ edit (module L1-2; record R15). TE's norm kernel, in the same
  fast-math build (module L26), flushes subnormal results. Subnormal gradient elements make no difference: their squares
  are below the smallest fp32 subnormal and add +0 on both sides. On the domain above the local norm could differ in its
  last bits, and with clipping active (c < 1) so could every update of that step; nothing would raise.

## Optimizer and gradient clipping (Optimizer, Gradient clipping)

### Optimizer

**Stock:** Megatron-Core's `DistributedOptimizer` with TE's `FusedAdam` in AdamW mode, fp32 master weights and moments,
bf16 parameters, configured in `pretrain.py` L327-340.

| Hyperparameter | Value | Where set |
|---|---|---|
| β1, β2 | 0.9, 0.95 | `pretrain.py` L334-335 |
| ε | 1e-5 | `pretrain.py` L336 |
| Weight decay λ | 0.1 | `pretrain.py` L331 (scheduler: constant 0.1, L357-358) |
| Gradient clip | 1.0 | `pretrain.py` L338 |
| Peak LR | 4e-4 | `config_GB300_2x4x2xtp1pp1cp1_8b.sh` L16 |
| Warm-up | 16 steps | same file, L17 |
| Schedule | cosine to LR / 10 | `pretrain.py` L354; `conf/custom.yaml` L188 (`min_lr`) |

These match the llama31_8b rows of the rules' hyperparameter table and the logged MLLOG keys (`result_1.txt` L98-109).

**The X9 update.** Per element of a shard; `c` is Megatron's clip coefficient and `t` the step. Every operation is fp32
with TE's fast-math rounding: FTZ, `div.full`, `sqrt.approx`.

```
ĝ      = c · fp32(g)                        mul.rn.ftz
m      = β1·m + (1−β1)·ĝ                    fma(β1, m, mul(1−β1, ĝ))
v      = β2·v + (1−β2)·ĝ·ĝ                  fma(β2, v, mul(mul(1−β2, ĝ), ĝ))
m̂      = m / bc1,  v̂ = v / bc2              div.full.ftz;  bc_i = fp32(1 − fp32(β_i)^t), computed in double
u      = m̂ / (sqrt(v̂) + ε) + λ·p            sqrt.approx.ftz, add, div.full, fma(λ, p, ·)   (decoupled weight decay)
p      = p − lr·u                            fma(lr · −1.0, u, p)   (a true negation of lr)
p_bf16 = bf16(p)                             round to nearest even
```

The real-valued form, which NVIDIA's chain also computes, is AdamW with bias correction:
`m_t = β1·m_{t−1} + (1−β1)·c·g_t`; `v_t = β2·v_{t−1} + (1−β2)·(c·g_t)²`;
`p_t = p_{t−1} − η_t·[(m_t/(1−β1^t)) / (√(v_t/(1−β2^t)) + ε) + λ·p_{t−1}]`.

- **Constants:** TE's host scalars (module L106-123): β rounded to fp32 first, `1 − β` in fp32, the bias corrections as
  stated; lr, ε and λ rounded to fp32 on the host (module L670-674).
- **References:** the chain is TE's `multi_tensor_adam` (ADAM_MODE_1, AdamW), operation for operation.
  `apex.optimizers.FusedAdam` with `adam_w_mode=True` is the same algorithm, and apex also compiles its multi-tensor
  kernels with `--use_fast_math`. The A/B under Evidence compares the kernel directly with both. ε placement, the
  weight-decay form and the clip application are unchanged, so no Equivalence exceptions (TR-9.5) exception is involved.
- **The warm-up.** NVIDIA's warm-up runs the optimizer with betas `[1, 1]`, no bias correction, lr 0 and weight decay 0,
  then restores the values and resets the step to 1. The kernel reads these values live from the parameter groups (`callback_warmup.py` L237-245, L300-313; the hook passes them at patch `mcore/0001` L274-280).

### Gradient clipping

- **The coefficient** is Megatron's: total norm = sqrt(all-reduce(Σ local_norm²)), `c = min(1, max_norm / (total +
  1e-6))`, `max_norm = 1.0`. With X9 armed it is computed by Megatron's own `clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32`, which the
  patch lets stash it, or by the patch's `clip_grad_norm` override with the same two fp32 operations on the device
  tensor (patch `mcore/0002` L75-78; patch `mcore/0001` L184-187). K6 does not compute it.
- **X9 changes only how the local norm is computed** (TE's exact reduction order; `c` has TE's bytes outside the norm's
  stated domain) and where `c` is applied: inside the fused step (`ĝ = c · g`), the same single fp32 multiply as TE's
  scale kernel's `float(g) · c` on the fp32 copies. Clipping is not deferred and not computed from partial data;
  normalisation is unchanged.
- **The gradients that enter the norm** are byte-identical to stock (K5, K13; N4 outside its stated domain, in which a
  census of one whole run found 0 elements; N7 up to the sign of exact zeros, which squares to the same value).

## Inputs it accepts (Shape specialisation)

### Gate

Shard sizes: any; the launch tables are built from the shard list.

- **Arms** (patch `mcore/0001` L119-123) on `AK_X9_E0=1`, the module loaded, not a stub optimizer, not Megatron-FSDP,
  no precision-aware optimizer, no reuse of the gradient buffer for an MXFP8 parameter gather; otherwise the stock chain
  runs.
- **Raises** when the gradient buffer is not bf16 (patch `mcore/0001` L134); a parameter is quantized (L207); a separate
  gradient-norm group exists, which would need a second clip coefficient (L212-214); the optimizer state is missing or
  not fp32 (L237-238); no clip coefficient was stashed before the fused step (L262); the weight-amax buffer belongs to
  another optimizer (L292-293); fp32 model parameters carry gradients (L170-171); in the module: a shard not contiguous
  or the lists not aligned (module L512), wrong dtypes (L515-516), an empty or non-bf16 gradient in the norm (L578), a
  slot list or amax buffer of the wrong shape or dtype (L663).
- **Falls back to stock, by design:** with no gradients bound since the last fused step, the stock master-to-bf16 copy
  runs (patch `mcore/0001` L97-102); with any non-bf16 gradient in the norm's list, TE's `multi_tensor_l2norm` runs
  (patch `mcore/0002` L55-61); before N6's weight-amax table is built, the step runs without the epilogue and N6 runs
  the shard pass (patch `mcore/0001` L288-291; `firmus/ak/pkg/ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L448-449).
  In the submitted runs the last case is the warm-up's first optimizer step; the epilogue first appears in the second
  (`result_1.txt` L929).

### Assumptions not checked in code

- **The optimizer is AdamW (decoupled weight decay).** The kernel implements AdamW only. Kept true by the recipe
  (`pretrain.py` L327-340), which uses Megatron-Core's default `decoupled_weight_decay=True`; every result log prints it
  (`result_1.txt` L404). If it failed: silent wrong result; with L2-style Adam the fused step would compute AdamW.
- **`capturable` is off.** No package file sets the optimizer's `capturable` or Megatron's `optimizer_cuda_graph`, and
  every log prints `optimizer_cuda_graph=False` (`result_1.txt` L405). If it failed: the effect is not analysed; the
  hook does not decline it.
- **TE's `step()` has run before the fused step in the same optimizer step**, so the group's step counter
  (`group["step"]`, used for the bias corrections) is already advanced and the state exists. Kept true by Megatron,
  which runs the inner optimizer's `step()` and then the master-to-bf16 copy, in whose place the fused step runs, only
  after gradients were bound in the same step (patch `mcore/0001` L97-109). The state's presence and dtype are asserted (L237-238); the counter is not. The closed loops ran N5's call pattern against stock `FusedAdam` for 2,002 steps, E0 at every step.
  If it failed: silent wrong result (a stale bias correction).
- **The cached gradient views, per-group lists and parameter-buffer views stay valid.** The hook builds them once and
  passes the same list objects every step; the module rebuilds its tables only when handed different list objects whose
  addresses differ (module L500-508, L565-575), so it relies on Megatron's buffers not moving. Kept true by: they are
  not reallocated during training in this recipe; the in-training shadows compared the live step with TE's chain on clones of the live buffers and found byte identity at every checked step, the last at step 1,536 of the 2 × 4 test run.
  If it failed: silent wrong result (reads and writes through stale addresses).
- **The stock chain's fp32 copies are 16-byte aligned**, so TE's aligned l2norm path is taken exactly when the length
  is a multiple of 4; the norm pass reproduces that choice (module L579-584). Kept true by: the stock copies are fresh
  allocations (`shard_model_grad.float()`). If it failed: the norm pass's order would no longer be the stock chain's
  for the affected shards, and the norm could differ in its last bits (no raise).
- **No partial sum of the norm is a nonzero fp32 subnormal** (Numerics). Nothing enforces it; no compared case or step
  showed a difference (Equivalence). If it failed: silent last-bit difference in the local norm, and with clipping
  active in every update of that step.

### Benchmark detection

The arithmetic does not depend on the data, the benchmark or the step's position: the kernels read the
hyperparameters live from the parameter groups and specialise only on shard sizes and addresses (the launch tables).
K6 does no benchmark detection (Benchmark detection, TR-2.3).

## How it is switched on and checked at run time (Enablement)

- **Switches** (read at import; default off): `AK_X9_E0` (patch `mcore/0001` L27), `AK_X9_WAMAX` (L52, only with
  `AK_X9_E0`), `AK_X9_FOLD` (patch `mcore/0002` L21), all set in the leaf (config L20).
  `AK_X9_EARLY_AG=1` (L47), the early parameter all-gather, is N5's switch.
- **Kernel directory:** `AK_X9_KERNEL_DIR`, default `/opt/firmus/ak/x9` (patch `mcore/0001` L30, patch `mcore/0002`
  L25), also set by the Dockerfile (L131). The module is imported with the patched files (patch `mcore/0001` L33-34,
  patch `mcore/0002` L28); a missing module raises there.
- **Run-time checks.** Each line below is printed by rank 0 only, so only rank 0's line reaches the log.
  - Norm pass: an ARMED line at the first call (patch `mcore/0002` L36-44), with the module's sha and no verdict. The
    run-start gate's `x9 norm fold` row (`firmus/ak/pkg/firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L105-108) passes once the norm
    pass has run on that rank; it compares no bytes. The gate's verdict is per rank
    ([Enablement and fail-loud behaviour](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)).
  - Fused step: an ARMED line at the first fused step (patch `mcore/0001` L253-257), with the module's sha and no
    verdict. The step has no run-time first-call check, and no gate row covers it.
  - Epilogue: the slot count (L297-300). At the first step with the epilogue (the warm-up's second optimizer step), N6
    recomputes the amaxes with the shard pass, compares the int32 bit patterns of every weight's amax before the
    all-reduce, prints the verdict and raises on any difference (`firmus/ak/pkg/ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L430-447). This
    runs once per run; later steps are not checked in the run.

## Approval (Approval)

- **Hyperparameters, optimizer paragraph (TR-9.1c).** An alternate optimizer implementation must describe the
  optimizer's equation and demonstrate equivalence with the approved optimizers. The rules' appendix of compliant
  optimizers lists `apex.optimizers.FusedAdam` for large language models in PyTorch; TE's `FusedAdam`, which NVIDIA's
  recipe uses, is not on that list. The equations are under Optimizer; the A/B compares the kernel with both: 0
  differing bytes.
- **Numerical formats (TR-5.2b).** Gradient clipping and normalisation are unchanged; the real-valued function is
  unchanged; only the handling of subnormal partial sums in the norm pass differs from TE's, on the stated domain, in
  which no test found a difference (Equivalence, "Class: E0-restricted").
- **Graph Execution (TR-8.3).** A different evaluation of the same computation: the same operations with the same
  rounding in the same order, byte-identical except on the stated norm domain.
- No exception is requested: no epsilon, weight-decay or clipping change, so no Equivalence exceptions (TR-9.5)
  exception is needed.

K6's ARMED lines and the epilogue check `True`; the equivalence tests ran on L4 v2's image, which carries the same kernel
file (`3035ea35`) and the same two patches (below).

- **The kit for this kernel, re-targeted at this image** (record R17): PASS, as written and after a random-byte fill of
  PyTorch's memory pools; one of the 24 re-targeted kits, 48 / 48 PASS. It checks the installed kernel file against the

  verifier's random-byte memory fill: subnormal-gradient and `−0.0` master cases, subnormal optimizer state, the
  warm-up's lr-0 step, non-finite values and offset views. Master, m, v, the bf16 parameters, the gradient norm and the
  clip coefficient (which the task computes from the norm with its own torch code, Megatron's formula): 0 differing
  bytes against the stock chain. The task grades the norm and the step without the epilogue.
- **A/B against TE's and apex's `FusedAdam`** (record R1): one GB300; the image's kernel against
  `transformer_engine.pytorch.optimizers.FusedAdam` and `apex.optimizers.FusedAdam`, both with `adam_w_mode=True`;
  identical inputs from zero optimizer state, fresh gradients at each of 100 steps; shards of 1,048,581, 65,536, 4,099,
  513 and 1 elements (1,118,730 in all: aligned, unaligned, ragged and single-element tails). The recipe's AdamW (β
  (0.9, 0.95), ε 1e-5, λ 0.1) with lr 4e-4 and clip coefficient 1.0; lr 4e-4 and 0.37; an edge case (bf16-subnormal
  gradients, ±0.0 and tiny masters); lr 0. X9 forms `c · fp32(g)` itself; the references step an fp32 master whose
  `.grad` is `fp32(g) · c` and take `master.to(bfloat16)` as the bf16 parameter. **Result:** X9 v TE, X9 v apex and TE
  v apex, over the fp32 master, m, v and the bf16 parameter, after steps 1, 2, 16 and 100: **192 comparisons, 0
  differing bytes**, max absolute and max relative difference 0.
- **In-training shadow, 2 × 4 test run** (record R2): the submitted configuration, 1,536 steps, with two test-only mounts
  (shadow hooks added to the installed `distrib_optimizer.py`; a matching test copy of the stack record, so the banner
  still checked every other file). On the warm-up's optimizer steps, the first seven steps of training, every 250th step
  and the last, every rank re-ran TE's own chain (fp32 copies, `multi_tensor_l2norm`, `multi_tensor_scale_tensor`,
  `multi_tensor_adam`) and the X9 kernel on clones of its shard and compared both with the live step (early all-gather
  and epilogue armed). **16 of 16 steps pass on all 8 ranks:** masters, moments, bf16 parameters (about 1.0 × 10⁹
  elements per rank per step), gradient norms and clip coefficient byte-identical.
- **Bundle-wide grading of the image** (record R7): **PASS**: every route graded the image's own `fused_adamw_master.py`
  (sha `3035ea35`, the file the runs loaded) byte-equal to the stock chain on every case of the training family, and
  every check ran: the call-site task and a unit test, each PASS, also under the address-independence and
  mixed-sequence checks (no capture-and-replay step: training runs the optimizer step eagerly); the kit, PASS. A
  coverage check lists all three called paths (the step, the norm pass, the epilogue) as graded (record R8).
- **Closed loops** (record R9): six loops of 2,002 optimizer steps (the recipe's 2 warm-up steps plus 2,000 on its
  schedule), one GPU, stock TE `FusedAdam` with Megatron's scale step against K6 called as N5 calls it; master, m, v,
  the bf16 parameter buffer, the gradient norm, the clip coefficient and the epilogue's amaxes compared after every
  step. **E0 in all six:** 12 synthetic shards; data-parallel rank 0 of 8 with 44 shards (the L4 run log's layout: 6
  shards in phase 1, 30 weight slots, 130 weights); rank 1 with 19; rank 7 with 12 shards and every 97th master `−0.0`;
  rank 0 with weight decay on; rank 0 with it off. In each loop the clip coefficient was below 1 on 160-168 steps, and
  10 % of rows had zero gradients (half +0, half −0). Controls: stock against stock E0; an earlier X9 kernel and a
  variant with `.ftz` stripped both caught, at steps 550-614, where moments decay into subnormals.
- **In-training shadow at DP 8** (record R10): graph mode, 36 shadowed steps per rank on every shard of every rank (12
  to 45 shards per rank): 0 mismatches in the fused step, the epilogue and the norm pass. The earlier-kernel control was
  caught on the four ranks that hold the embedding's shards (first at step 480), whose zero-gradient rows have moments
  decaying into subnormals. Eager mode: 18 steps, 0 mismatches. In graph mode the optimizer step is the part of the
  iteration that runs eagerly, so K6 and N5 are the items shadowed in graph mode.
- **Captured training tensors** (record R11): cases captured on rank 0 of a stock DP-8 run to its final evaluation (the
  warm-up's steps, steps 1 and 2 and every capture step, both parameter groups): 17 / 17 E0, and 17 / 17 synthetic
  cases E0. Rank 0's slices hold no zero-gradient parameter (it holds no embedding shard) and no subnormal, NaN or Inf
  value. A deliberately wrong control kernel (it changes masters above a threshold) was caught: 9 of 17 differ.
- **The verifier's stricter checks** (record R12): E0 with fresh contents for every timed call (speed ratio 2.617 over
  the stock chain); the cached launch tables pass the cross-call state check only under their declared name
  (`x9_launch_tables`), and without the declaration the verifier rejects them; the launch check saw 10 GPU activities
  per call, all on one stream, with no host synchronisation; with every check on, E0 on 90 cases (17 visible, 17
  reseeded, 34 hidden, 16 shape variants, 6 edge). The state and launch checks are outside the verifier's default
  checks; passing the state check says the cached state has a declared name, not that it is harmless.
